note: DESIGN ONLY. No product features implemented. Structure is traceable to VSA-1..10 / CPM-1..10 per Policy v1.2.

step57_repositoryStructure.principle: Feature-first slice ownership (VSA-6) with a deliberately small platform (VSA-2). Directory layout makes ownership visible: if you cannot tell who owns a file from its path, the layout has failed.

topLevel.rule: One directory per vertical slice. A slice is the smallest independently testable capability spanning all layers (VSA-1).
Approved shared platform only. Deliberately small; every addition is a governed promotion (VSA-2).
Versioned, directional, acyclic public contracts. The ONLY permitted cross-slice dependency path (VSA-3).
Canonical shared data foundations — migrations, seeds, field catalog. Platform-owned, DDR-governed (VSA-4).
Migrations runner, jobs, ingestion, materializations, deployment artifacts. Every artifact version-controlled with named ownership (VSA-8).
Configuration hierarchy and environment overrides. Never contains secret values.
Cross-cutting test suites. Slice-owned tests live inside the slice (VSA-6).
Documentation by audience with explicit update triggers.
Frozen Agent Framework v1 baseline, profile, adapters, evidence. Read-mostly.
CODEOWNERS, workflows, branch protection config, PR/issue templates. This is where the declarative tool-permission matrix becomes ENFORCED.

step57_repositoryStructure.acyclicityRule: Dependency direction is one-way: slices -> contracts -> platform -> data. A slice never imports another slice directly; platform never imports a slice (VSA-3).
step57_repositoryStructure.reviewStatus: Architecture-reviewed against VSA-1..10; traceability recorded per directory

step58_sliceStructure.principle: Each slice owns its full stack. Everything needed to test the slice independently lives inside it (VSA-1).

contents.desc: Slice-owned business logic and feature policy (VSA-5: slices own feature policy)
Slice-owned data objects ONLY. Canonical shared data is platform-owned and lives in /data (VSA-4)
Slice-owned components; consumes the design system, never forks it
unit/, integration/, contract/ — slice-owned, runnable in isolation
REQUIRED. Declares slice id, owner role, consumed contracts (with versions), produced contracts, platform extension points used, lifecycle state, and risk class.

step58_sliceStructure.manifestRule: A slice without a valid slice.manifest.json is not a slice — it is ungoverned code. The manifest is what makes ownership and dependencies machine-checkable rather than conventional.
step58_sliceStructure.boundaryRule: Cross-slice import is a build failure, not a code review comment. Enforced by a deterministic check in CI (Step 69).

step59_platformStructure.principle: The shared platform stays deliberately small (VSA-2). Small is the feature, not a limitation — the cost of changing shared things is why they must be few.

contents.desc: Tenant context resolution and isolation enforcement
Data access foundations; every path tenant-scoped
Logging, metrics, tracing; never logs secrets
Design tokens and theme registry. Appearance only — no feature logic (UX/theming policy)
Declared extension points slices bind to (VSA-5)

step59_platformStructure.promotionRule: Moving code into platform/ is a governed promotion requiring architecture review, impact analysis, consumer identification, retest of affected consumers, and human approval (MATERIAL_ARCHITECTURE_SHARED_PLATFORM). Convenience is never a promotion basis.
step59_platformStructure.prohibition: Platform must not absorb feature behaviour. If a change to platform/ is driven by one slice's requirement, that is a signal the code belongs in the slice.

hierarchy: config/environments/<env>/ — per-environment overrides, committed, no secrets
runtime injection — secret VALUES only, never committed, never logged
step60_configuration.secretsRule: Configuration files contain secret NAMES/references only. Secret VALUES arrive at runtime through an injection interface the application reads and no agent ever sees. This is architecture, not exception — secret_protection is a global non-waivable invariant.
step60_configuration.validationRule: Every configuration surface has a schema. Startup fails loudly on an invalid or incomplete configuration; it never starts with a silently defaulted security-relevant value.
step60_configuration.safeDefaultRule: Defaults fail closed: absent configuration yields the most restrictive behaviour, never the most permissive.

step61_testStructure.principle: Test location follows ownership. Slice-owned tests live in the slice; cross-cutting suites live centrally (VSA-6/VSA-7).

central.desc: Cross-slice contract conformance — verifies VSA-3 directionality and versioning
Auth/authz, secret handling, dependency and static security scans
Tenant isolation — every canonical access path proven tenant-scoped
Visual regression baselines and accessibility checks; deterministic output required
Performance contracts against versioned representative workloads
Shared fixtures. Chart/widget fixtures must cover: zero rows, one row, all-equal, extreme outlier, long labels, too many categories, negatives, nulls mid-series
The framework's own regression portfolios, runnable independently of application code

step61_testStructure.verificationMapLink: Test locations map to the 360-decision verification map: each decision's required evidence class resolves to a concrete suite here, so evidence is linkable by decision ID.

structure.updateTrigger: Any change to build, run, or test procedure
Any approved architecture decision or contract version change
Any public contract change — same PR, not later
Any canonical data or field catalog change
Any deployment, job, or recovery procedure change
Any data contract or onboarding procedure change
Every gate closure — evidence is linked, not narrated
Every major run and before any context transition

step62_documentation.rule: Documentation never creates or changes a decision. It reflects an approved source. Where documentation and its governing source diverge, the source wins and the divergence is a defect.
